title: Chronic Kidney Disease Of Uncertain Etiology In Agricultural Communities
summary: Build a verified measurement workflow for identifying chronic kidney disease of uncertain etiology in agricultural and other manual-worker communities, separating persistent kidney disease from transient acute kidney injury and traditional causes before any exposure or prevention decision is made.
why_it_matters: A Ministry of Health NCD or occupational-health director, labor ministry, or health funder must decide whether to invest in sentinel kidney surveillance, primary-care screening, worker heat and hydration protections, safe-water investigation, or broader exposure studies. WHO estimates 674 million people live with chronic kidney disease, most in low- and middle-income countries, while recent CKDu work reports that cross-region burden is poorly described, terminology is inconsistent, and exposure measurement often relies on self-report. Regional primary studies found CKDu in 2.66% of 3,350 agricultural workers in Tamil Nadu and suspected CKDu in 8.5% of a selected rural Sri Lankan population, but these estimates are not interchangeable. A verified cross-setting measurement layer could change which surveillance and prevention evidence a decision-maker funds; it must not be converted into a causal attribution or worker-protection order before replication.

success_metrics.target: Every analyzed setting records whether CKD was confirmed with repeat kidney-function testing at least 90 days apart and how transient AKI or single low eGFR results were handled.
success_metrics.validation_method: Reviewer checks the case-definition crosswalk against source methods, laboratory timing, and exclusion rules.

success_metrics.target: Every CKDu/CINAC label records the operational definition, traditional-risk-factor exclusions, proteinuria or albuminuria field, and whether the label is suspected, probable, or confirmed.
success_metrics.validation_method: Domain reviewer compares each classification field with the original study protocol and records non-comparable definitions.

success_metrics.target: Heat, hydration, water, agrochemical, medication, and infection exposures are separated by instrument, timing, and measurement mode; self-report is never treated as objective exposure proof.
success_metrics.validation_method: Data-quality review checks exposure provenance, recall window, missingness, and whether biological or environmental measurements were actually collected.

success_metrics.target: No causal, clinical, worker-protection, or resource-allocation output is published without domain review, red-team review, and independent replication.
success_metrics.validation_method: Review records and replication artifacts are checked before any output moves beyond discovery or analytic framing.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, nephrology or occupational-health domain review, red-team review for causal or worker-protection interpretation, field-reality review for operational outputs, and independent replication for quantitative results.
